Read the figure. Arc abcd is a certain latitude circle, o is the center of the circle, a and c are the two intersections of the twilight line with this latitude, and b and d are respectively the midpoints of arc abc and arc adc. Read the figure and answer the question.

<image1>

If the rotational linear velocity at place a is about half of the rotational linear velocity at the equator, the local time is 2h earlier than Greenwich time, and ∠aoc=130°, then what might the latitude of place c be?

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a circular latitude circle, with O near the center of the circle; point a is located at the upper left of the circumference, point c is located at the upper right of the circumference, and point b is below on the circumference; O is connected respectively to a, c, and b. d is marked at the middle position of the upper arc from a to c. It can be seen from the figure that the direction from a along the upper shorter arc to c is clockwise on the plane of the figure, and this shorter arc corresponds to central angle ∠AOC=130°.

Then reason: a and c are on the same latitude circle, so their latitudes are the same. The rotational linear velocity at place a is about half of the linear velocity at the equator. According to the formula v=v_equator·cosφ, cosφ≈1/2, so the absolute value of the latitude of this latitude circle is 60°, and therefore place c can only be 60°N or 60°S. The local time at place a is 2 hours earlier than Greenwich time, indicating that the longitude of place a is 30°E. If the 130° shorter arc from a to c in the figure is the eastward direction, the direction in which local time increases, then c is 130° east of a, with longitude 160°E. In a polar view of a latitude circle, eastward in the Northern Hemisphere appears counterclockwise, and eastward in the Southern Hemisphere appears clockwise; while the eastward direction from a to c in the figure is clockwise, so this latitude circle is located in the Southern Hemisphere. Therefore, the latitude of place c is 60°S.
